title: Recognize CRLF historical hooks without overwriting custom checks
goal: Upgrade Windows-managed Throughline hooks to fail-fast branch enforcement without mistaking project-owned hook composition for plugin ownership.
in_scope: Normalize CRLF and LF line endings before matching known historical Throughline hook content
Refresh only exact normalized matches for current or known historical managed hooks
Preserve composed hooks that contain Throughline commands plus any additional executable project checks
Verify a refreshed historical hook cannot mask a failed branch check behind a later successful validator
Keep scripts/sync-plugin.mjs and the bootstrap scaffold copy behaviorally identical
out_of_scope: Parsing or rewriting arbitrary shell hook logic
Changing the seed-only policy for project-owned workflow files
acceptance: sync-plugin.mjs normalizes line endings when comparing a live pre-commit hook with every known Throughline-managed historical hook, so a CRLF copy refreshes to the current fail-fast hook while a composed or custom hook with any additional executable content remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is reported for manual review; the self-hosted and shipped scaffold copies behave identically.
invariants: Line-ending differences alone do not change managed-hook ownership
Additional executable content always makes the live hook project-owned
Project-owned hooks are never overwritten without explicit force or manual action
Managed hooks stop on a failed protected-branch check
